theme.label: Color theme
lang.label: Interface language
conn.title: Connections
conn.name: Name
conn.keychain: Passwords are kept in the system keychain (Windows Credential Manager / Secret Service), never in the Cmdex database. The server's key is checked against ~/.ssh/known_hosts.
conn.telnetWarn: Telnet is not encrypted: passwords and data travel in plain text. Use it only on a trusted local network.
conn.serialNone: No serial port found. Plug the adapter in and open this form again.
conn.deleteQ: Delete the connection "{name}" and its stored password?
conn.trustText: Cmdex has never connected to {host}. This is its key fingerprint:
conn.trustHint: If you can, compare it with the server's (ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub). Trusting adds it to ~/.ssh/known_hosts; if it ever changes, Cmdex will refuse to connect.
ask.label: What do you want to do?
ask.placeholder: Describe a task, or paste a command to see what it means…   (Ctrl+K)
mode.autoExplain: This looks like a command, so it is explained. Enter runs it.
mode.autoSearch: Paste a command here to see what each part means.
mode.forced: Keeping the mode you picked — type to switch automatically again.
search.found: {n} commands · most relevant first, those for {s} ahead
build.title: Build
build.pick: Pick a command in the suggestions below to build it here.
run.done: Pasted into {s}: check it, then press Enter in the terminal to run it.
run.pasteHint: Pastes the command into the terminal without running it: you press Enter.
risk.1hint: Changes the system (services, packages, firewall, users, configuration).
risk.2hint: May delete data or cut service (recursive delete, format, restart, wiping a configuration).
risk.2note: Critical: this can delete data or cut service. Check every part before pressing Enter.
explain.missing: Nothing is known yet about: {list}. Save the command to the library and add notes, or edit the explanation.
explain.source: Explanations come from your library and from the help already on this computer (man, Get-Help, /?). Italic labels are guesses.
collect.title: Collected while you work
collect.lead: Cmdex reads the commands you run, hides secrets, turns values into parameters and groups lines that differ only in values. Nothing enters your library until you approve it.
collect.step1d: Shell history and commands run through Cmdex.
collect.step2d: Passwords, tokens and keys become •••••• before anything is stored.
collect.step3d: IPs, hosts, ports, paths and numbers become {parameters}.
collect.step4d: Same template: one group. Like a saved command: merge offered.
collect.step5d: Grouped by your rules, waiting for your review.
collect.empty: Nothing to review. Commands you run will show up here.
collect.secret: secret hidden — the value is never stored
collect.added: Added to the library — rename it there.
collect.src.sessionNote: ▶ Run and the command box; never what you type at a password prompt
collect.noHistory: No shell history file found for this user.
collect.privacy: Everything collected stays on this computer. The lines as you ran them (folders included) are never put in a shared pack; a full backup does hold them.
collect.autoMergeNote: A command that resembles one in your library at least as much as the level below is merged into it. New commands still wait for you.
collect.levelNote: Also the level from which a merge is suggested. 100% = only the same template.
collect.clearQ: Delete the command lines collected so far and the groups waiting for review? Your library is not touched, and what you already added, merged or ignored stays decided.
collect.clearNote: Turn off "Collect commands" above if you do not want new ones.
collect.autoMerged: {n} collected groups merged into your library automatically.
rules.title: Classification rules
lib.title: Library
filter.label: Systems:
filter.hidesSession: the filter hides {p}, the active session's system
lib.reimportQ: Bring back the starter commands you deleted? Commands you changed stay as they are.
lib.empty: Your library is empty. Add a command, import a file, or turn on collecting.
lib.defaultHint: Comes with Cmdex and is updated with it. Saving a change makes it your own copy, which updates never touch.
lib.editedDefault: your copy of a starter command ({p})
lib.editedHint: You changed this starter command; updates of Cmdex keep your version. Delete it to drop it.
lib.name: Name
lib.templateHint: Put parameters in curly braces, e.g. ping {host} -n {count}. A row appears for each.
lib.safety2: Critical: deletes data or cuts service
ex.title: What "{p}" means
ex.letters: Single letters that combine, like -ano (a=all; n=numeric)
ex.hint: Options are matched as written (Linux: -L and -l differ), then in any case (Windows: /FI = /fi).
update.title: Cmdex {v} is available
update.text: You have {cur}. The new version is downloaded from GitHub, checked against its published checksum, installed, and Cmdex restarts.
db.errorTitle: The database could not be opened
lock.title: Unlock your library
lock.createText: Your library is encrypted. This computer has no password keyring (Secret Service) to keep its key, so Cmdex asks for a master password at each start instead. Choose one of at least 10 characters and keep it safe: without it the library cannot be opened.
lock.newPassword: New master password (10 characters or more)
lock.differ: The two passwords differ. Try again.
lock.forgot: Without the master password the library cannot be opened. You can try again, or start a new library: the locked one is renamed and kept.
lock.lostTitle: The key of your library is missing
lock.lostText: Your library ({p}) is encrypted, and its key is not in this computer's keychain: the database comes from another computer or user, or the keychain was reset. Restore it from a JSON backup (Library ▸ Import), or start a new library: the locked one is renamed and kept.
lock.freshQ: The locked library is renamed (…locked-<date>) and kept, and Cmdex starts with a new, empty one. Continue?
io.kind.db: A Cmdex database file (.db). It is read from a copy; the file itself is not changed.
io.kind.pack: A command pack (JSON). Its commands are added to your library.
io.modes: Merge: keep everything here and add what is missing; a command edited more recently in the file replaces the older copy. Replace: empty this library first, then load the file.
io.replaceQ: Everything in this library (commands, explanations, rules, connections, collected lines, settings) will be replaced by the file. Export a backup first if you may need it. Continue?
io.done: {added} commands added, {updated} updated, {kept} already here; {explains} explanations, {rules} rules, {connections} connections, {collected} collected groups, {settings} settings. {rejected} refused because they hide control or invisible characters.
io.exp.backupD: everything — commands, explanations, rules, synonyms, connections, collected lines, settings — in a readable JSON file. Best for moving to another computer.
io.exp.dbD: an exact copy of the SQLite database. Its private values stay encrypted with this computer's key, so it imports only here (Import…).
io.exp.packD: only commands, explanations, synonyms and rules, to share with others.
io.noPasswords: Passwords are never exported: they stay in this computer's keychain. On the new computer Cmdex asks for them at the first connection.
link.title: Open a link from the terminal?
link.text: The session printed a link to {url}. It opens in your web browser, not in Cmdex. Open it only if you trust it.
run.hidden: This command contains hidden or control characters, so it was not run.
kp.title: Secure entry
kp.empty: Click the keys below; the physical keyboard is not used
kp.hint: Keys move after every click, and the window is hidden from screen capture while this is open, so neither a keylogger nor a screenshot can read what you enter.
conn.rememberQ: Keep it in the system keychain so Cmdex does not ask again?
term.secretHint: For sudo, su or Password: prompts: entered on the secure keypad, sent with Enter, never stored.
protect.on: Screen-capture protection ON: screenshots, recordings and screen sharing do not see Cmdex. Click to turn off.
protect.off: Screen-capture protection OFF. Click to hide Cmdex from screenshots, recordings and screen sharing.
protect.unsupported: Screen-capture protection needs Windows 10 (2004) or later; Linux has no way to offer it.
settings.title: Settings
settings.autostart: Open Cmdex when I sign in to {os}
settings.autostartHint: for this account only, no administrator rights
settings.autostartOn: On: {p} opens when you sign in.
settings.autostartOff: Off: Cmdex opens only when you open it.
settings.autostartNo: This development build cannot start at sign-in; use the installed Cmdex.
tools.title: Tool packs
tools.lead: Commands for programs such as nmap or python. They are built into Cmdex, so nothing is downloaded. Cmdex offers a pack when it finds the program on PATH, and it only looks at file names, never runs the program.
tools.none: This version of Cmdex has no tool packs yet.
tools.note: Turning a pack off removes its commands. Commands you edited stay in your library.
tools.offerText: Cmdex found {name} on this computer. Add its pack of {n} commands to the library?
map.modeHint: Your folders as a galaxy. Hover a star for details; click a folder to fly in.
map.tip.moreText: {n} more items, not drawn to keep the map light
map.tip.notRead: not read yet: click to open
map.hint: Click a star to choose it, right-click for file actions. Drag a star into the black hole to send it to the trash.
map.moreHint: Open the folder in the file manager to see them all.
map.trashQ: Send "{name}" into the black hole? It goes to the system trash and can be restored from there.
map.trashed: "{name}" went into the black hole (the trash).
map.runText: Opening "{name}" runs it as a program. Only continue if you trust it.
map.group.title: {n} chosen
map.group.trashQ: Throw these {n} items into the black hole? Folders go with everything inside (about {f} files). They go to the system trash and can be restored from there.
map.group.hint: Ctrl+click adds or removes a star. Shift+drag on the sky chooses every star in a box. Esc clears.
map.group.trashed: {n} items went into the black hole (the trash).
map.group.partial: {ok} went into the black hole; {bad} could not: {err}
notes.title: Notes
notes.empty: No notes yet. Write one below: text in any language, with formatting and images.
notes.deleteQ: Delete this note and its images?
notes.hint: Enter sends · Shift+Enter: new line · **bold** *italic* __underline__ ~~strike~~ ==highlight== `code` · # heading · - list · - [ ] task · > quote · paste or drop images
notes.attach: Pin to the file or folder chosen on the map
notes.attachNone: Open the map and choose a file or folder first.
notes.notImage: "{name}" is not a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image.
notes.fmt.heading: Heading
notes.copyCode: Copy the code (it is never run)
term.copyNothing: Select text first, or choose Copy everything.
term.pasteManyText: The clipboard holds {n} lines. Most shells run each line as soon as it is pasted. Check them first:
io.sealedAsk: This backup is protected. Its password:
io.protect.withD: encrypted (AES-256, key from your password with Argon2id). It opens on any computer, Windows or Linux, only with the password. If you forget it, the backup is lost.
io.protect.withoutD: plain JSON that anyone holding the file can read, notes and connections included. Keep it as safe as your computer.
io.protect.new: Choose the backup's password (at least 8 characters):
io.protect.short: The password needs at least 8 characters.
io.protect.differ: The two passwords differ. Try again.
mask.buttonHint: A copy of this terminal's output with secrets, addresses and names masked, for screen sharing
mask.title: Masked log
mask.viewerOn: The shared log window is open
mask.viewerHint: A separate window that only ever receives masked text. It is not protected from screen capture: share it instead of this window. Select text there and choose "Mask this too" to add a rule.
mask.viewerFail: Could not open the shared window: {err}
mask.catHint.secret: Passwords, tokens, API keys, Cisco password 7 / secret 5, PSK, SNMP communities, Wi-Fi keys, password hashes
mask.catHint.ip: IPv4 and IPv6 (masks such as 255.255.255.0, 0.0.0.0 and 127.x stay)
mask.catHint.serial: Serial Number, SN:, Processor board ID, UUID
mask.catHint.user: C:\Users\name, /home/name, user@host prompts, username / login as:, this computer's account
mask.catHint.host: This computer's name, hostname X, Host Name:, Device ID:, device prompts (Router#)
mask.catHint.domain: Any name that looks like a domain (example.com): masks a lot, including some that are not names
mask.valuePh: Text to mask, e.g. a customer name
mask.afterPh: Keyword, e.g. site-code: masks the word after it
mask.patternPh: RE2 pattern; group 1 (if any) is masked
mask.hideHint: Show •••••• instead of a name such as LABEL-1
mask.rulesHint: Rules only describe text to find: they never run anything. They are stored encrypted (a rule may be the secret itself) and travel with JSON backups.
mask.revealHint: The real values are shown only here, in the main window.
mask.revealUnprotected: Screen-capture protection is OFF: anyone watching this screen would see the real values.
mask.caveat: Masking by patterns is never complete: what no rule describes stays visible. Check the shared window before you share it. Full-screen programs (vim, top, less) are not logged. Everything is kept in memory only and erased when you close the tab.
mask.addedFromViewer: A rule was added from the shared window; the logs were masked again.
viewer.title: Cmdex · masked log
viewer.empty: No terminal is open in Cmdex.
viewer.maskShort: Select at least 3 characters on one line.
viewer.masked: Masked from now on, in every tab.
viewer.notice: Only masked text reaches this window. Masking by patterns is never complete: check before you share.
viewer.paused: Scrolled up: new lines wait below
